content.text:
I submitted composition **168** (Cu 0.37, Fe 0.26, V 0.38), which gave **6.32 µA**, the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured.

The merit budget allowed only 3 measurements across 297 compositions, so this was a sparse search. I don't know how close 168 is to the best in the library.

| Index | Cu / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 196 | 0.46 / 0.13 / 0.42 | 2.67 µA |
| **168** | **0.37 / 0.26 / 0.38** | **6.32 µA** |
| 102 | 0.35 / 0.34 / 0.32 | 2.93 µA |

- **How I chose:** I started in the Cu-rich region with 0.35–0.45 V because, from memory, copper vanadates absorb light at 2.72 eV. Nothing in this session confirmed that. I measured 196 and 168 together, saw that 168 (more Fe) was higher, and spent the last measurement on 102, which has even more Fe.
- **Pattern:** Photocurrent peaked at moderate Fe (about 0.26) and fell on either side. That comes from only three points along one direction, so it's suggestive at best.
- **Not explored:** the V-rich region (V above 0.6), the Fe-rich region, and the Cu-rich region with low V.
- **Unused budget:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements. They can't measure photocurrent directly, and I didn't use them to guide the choices.
